title: One event clock for 2D projectile motion

authority_basis.claim_scope: Horizontal and vertical component equations describe the same particle at the same elapsed time.

concepts.statement: The x and y component equations refer to the same projectile and therefore use the same elapsed time for a given event.
concepts.why_required: A 2D event is one physical state, not two independently timed component events.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners can solve x and y with incompatible times and combine states that never occur simultaneously.

model_conditions.condition: The horizontal and vertical equations refer to the same projectile event and the same time origin.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Component equations are coordinates of one state in the same trajectory.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Combining different event times creates a nonphysical state pair.

representations.semantic_geometry: A single timeline begins at release t=0 and terminates at a named event, with both x and y component relations attached to the same event marker.
must_not_imply: x and y motions possess independent clocks
representations.verification_method: Substitute the same event time into both component states and confirm the pair describes one trajectory event.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Name the physical event being solved for before selecting equations.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Different component conditions may accidentally refer to different events.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Define one common time origin for the projectile motion.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Elapsed times can be offset between the component descriptions.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Use the same event time in the horizontal and vertical component equations.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The computed x and y values can represent different states of the trajectory.

required_transformations.description: Map a physical event to one elapsed time shared by both component descriptions.
Bind x and y component results to the same event clock before interpreting the state.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Horizontal and vertical motions can use different times for the same projectile event.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The equations are often solved separately, which can make the component descriptions look like independent motions.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Pair an x-position computed at 1 s with a y-position computed at 2 s and show that no single projectile state can have both coordinates simultaneously.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Use one event timeline feeding both component equations.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Both component descriptions are coordinates of the same state at one elapsed time.
misconceptions.verification: Substitute the same t_event into both component equations and check event conditions simultaneously.

problem_families.name: Projectile special-event timing
problem_families.first_technical_move: Name the event and solve for its single elapsed time before transferring that time to the other component.

problem_families.name: Projectile intersection event
problem_families.first_technical_move: Express both event conditions using one common time parameter.
fatal_errors: solving x and y at unrelated times

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the shared-clock invariant from the gate.
